# Nahum

::: {.book-summary}
## Book Summary Insight

Nahum announces the fall of Nineveh and celebrates God's justice. The book teaches that God will ultimately judge evil and vindicate His people.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 1

<div class="key-verse">Nahum 1:7</div>

<div class="identifier">The LORD is good, a stronghold in the day of trouble</div>

### Why This Verse

Most quoted verse in Nahum

### Chapter Insight

This chapter proclaims God's justice, power, and goodness. The key verse emphasizes that while God judges evil, He is also a refuge for those who trust Him.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 2

<div class="key-verse">Nahum 2:3</div>

<div class="identifier">The shield of his mighty men is made red</div>

### Why This Verse

Vivid judgment imagery

### Chapter Insight

This chapter vividly describes the fall of Nineveh. The key verse highlights the certainty of God's judgment against oppressive powers.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 3

<div class="key-verse">Nahum 3:19</div>

<div class="identifier">There is no healing of thy bruise</div>

### Why This Verse

Final judgment on Nineveh

### Chapter Insight

This chapter explains the reasons for Nineveh's destruction. The key verse demonstrates that violence, cruelty, and pride ultimately bring divine judgment.
:::
